name: @clize/clize
stderr:
Usage: clize [options] [command]

Clize — the real-world capability layer for agents: identity & inbox · sites ·
domains · payments & storefront · media · SEO

Options:
  -V, --version                output the version number
  -h, --help                   display help for command

Commands:
  login [options]              log in: by default authorize in the browser with
                               GitHub / Google / email (hosted); --github uses
                               the device flow; --token is manual
  logout                       log out: remove the clize key saved on this
                               machine (~/.clize/config.json)
  install [options]            wire clize into the coding agents on this machine
                               (Claude Code / Codex / Pi / OpenClaw, and any
                               agent that reads ~/.agents/skills): installs the
                               skill by default; add --mcp to also register the
                               MCP server
  update [options]             update clize to the latest version and refresh
                               the skill (knows volta/asdf/nodenv/pnpm/bun;
                               verifies the running version after upgrading)
  doctor                       three-layer check-up: CLI (installed = running?)
                               / skill (what the agent knows) / control-plane
                               worker (which capabilities are live)
  check [domain]               connectivity self-check: verifies credentials /
                               account / a domain price lookup (read-only, free)
  claim [options] <slug>       claim a free handle <slug>.clize.app (first come,
                               first served; belongs to the checked-out project,
                               or to a project named after the handle when none
                               is checked out; inbound is off by default,
                               --email opens it too)
  release <slug>               release one of your free handles (deletes its
                               DNS, site content, mailboxes and inbound routing
                               + the identity; frees the name)
  init [options]               directory = project: bind an identity and check
                               out its project in one step (writes ./clize.json;
                               an identity you already claimed / bought binds to
                               the project it lives in, otherwise the project is
                               created on the first claim/buy)
  use <project>                switch the current directory to a project
                               (commands here then default to it; writes
                               ./clize.json)
  projects                     projects: list / create / move resources / rename
                               / remove (no subcommand = list)
  status [options]             workspace overview: domains, mailbox / site
                               status, this month's spend; --assets adds expiry
                               and health checks
  context [options] [address]  rehydrate at the start of a session: an address's
                               identity + knowledge + operating rules for the
                               agent's system prompt (no address = list
                               addresses)
  email                        email: setup / send / receive
  deploy [options] <path>      deploy: a multi-file static site to a free handle
                               or your own domain (no --domain needed in an
                               initialised directory)
  serve [options] [path]       local preview: a static server with Range support
                               that does not force no-store on media (use it for
                               sites / clips with video, not python -m
                               http.server)
  build                        make a piece of work end to end: build site =
                               site/UI · build clip
